bug_description.original: The vulnerability is that the gets() function in LibRaw_buffer_datastream does not always return a 0-terminated string, which can lead to issues in functions such as parse_rollei.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 127-byte buffer whose first 9 bytes are `DSC-Image` and whose remaining bytes are spaces. `LibRaw::identify()` reads the header, matches that Rollei signature, and dispatches to `LibRaw::parse_rollei()`. `parse_rollei()` rewinds the datastream and calls `fgets(line, 128, ifp)`, which expands to `LibRaw_buffer_datastream::gets(line, 128)`. Because the witness contains no newline, `gets()` copies bytes until EOF. Its copy loop uses `(pdest - str) < sz` instead of reserving one byte for a trailing NUL, so the loop can exit with `pdest == line + 127`. The post-loop guard `if ((pdest - str) < sz)` still passes at that state, and `*(++pdest) = 0` writes the terminator at `line[128]`, one byte past `parse_rollei()`'s 128-byte stack buffer. AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 in `LibRaw_buffer_datastream::gets`.

source.description: First project-side read on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled Rollei metadata bytes into the stack buffer that is later overflowed.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 127 bytes long, begins with ASCII `DSC-Image`, and contains no newline. After `identify()` dispatches on that header, `parse_rollei()` rewinds the stream and calls `fgets(line, 128, ifp)` on those same 127 bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled buffer length becomes `streamsize`. For the staged witness `bsize == 127`, and that EOF bound later determines that `gets()` exits with `pdest - str == 127` before attempting to append the trailing NUL.

root_cause.description: The copy loop treats all `sz` bytes as payload space instead of stopping at `sz - 1` to reserve room for the terminating NUL that the same function appends after the loop.
root_cause.note: On this witness there is no newline, so the loop exits only at EOF with `streamsize == 127`. That leaves `pdest - str == 127`, meaning `pdest` already points at the last in-bounds slot of `line[128]` before the post-loop terminator logic runs. The fix changes this bound, and the matching post-loop check, to `sz - 1`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After EOF leaves `pdest == line + 127`, the preincrement advances to `line + 128` and writes one byte past `parse_rollei()`'s 128-byte stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 1` here and identifies local object `line` in `LibRaw::parse_rollei()` as the overflowed stack region `[32,160)`.

parser_admitted.description: The first 9 bytes of the staged witness are `DSC-Image`, so `identify()` selects the Rollei parser and reaches the vulnerable `fgets(line, 128, ifp)` path.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness passes the staged 127-byte witness into `LibRaw::open_buffer()`.
LibRaw reads the header from the buffer-backed datastream, matches the Rollei signature `DSC-Image`, and dispatches to `parse_rollei()`.
The Rollei parser rewinds the datastream and requests one metadata line into stack `line[128]` with `fgets(line, 128, ifp)`.

Because the witness is 127 bytes long and contains no newline, `gets()` copies until EOF, leaves `pdest == line + 127`, and then overflows the stack buffer when its terminator write preincrements `pdest` and stores `0` at `line[128]`.

fine_trace.note: Source. After `identify()` has matched the Rollei signature and `parse_rollei()` has rewound the stream to offset 0, this `fgets` macro expands to `ifp->gets(line, 128)`. It asks the datastream to materialize the first metadata line into stack `line[128]`; the staged witness is 127 bytes long and has no `\n`, so the call will run to EOF.

The callee aliases the source to the beginning of the attacker-controlled buffer and the destination to the caller's stack array. On this call `streampos == 0` because `parse_rollei()` just sought to the start, and `streamsize == 127` because the staged PoC length was stored when `open_buffer()` wrapped the witness in `LibRaw_buffer_datastream`.

Root cause. The copy bound allows `pdest` to advance while `(pdest - str) < sz` instead of stopping at `sz - 1` to preserve room for a terminator. Because the witness contains no newline, the loop exits only when `psrc` reaches EOF at `streamsize == 127`, leaving `pdest - str == 127` and `pdest` already positioned at the last in-bounds slot of `line[128]`.

After step 3, the post-loop guard still evaluates `127 < 128` as true. It checks only the current offset and does not account for the next statement's preincrement, so it approves a terminator write even though `pdest` already points at the final in-bounds byte of `line`.

Sink. `++pdest` moves from `line + 127` to `line + 128`, and the store writes one byte past `parse_rollei()`'s 128-byte stack buffer. AddressSanitizer reports `WRITE of size 1` at this statement and ties the overflow to local object `line` in the caller frame.

allocation_context.note: AddressSanitizer identifies the overflowed stack frame at `parse_rollei` line 293 and reports local object `line` declared at line 294 occupying `[32,160)`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, the vulnerable checkout, and the saved witness bytes

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. AddressSanitizer says the overwritten object is stack-local `line` in `parse_rollei`, and fine-trace steps 1-5 show `pdest` aliasing that same buffer from the `fgets(line, 128, ifp)` call into the overflowing terminator write.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved AddressSanitizer stack is `gets -> parse_rollei -> identify -> open_datastream -> open_buffer`. Fine-trace step 5 is the top frame, fine-trace step 1 is the caller's `fgets` site in `parse_rollei`, and the parser_admitted checkpoint matches the `identify()` Rollei dispatch in frame 2.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The fix changes both the copy loop bound and the post-loop guard from `sz` to `sz - 1`, and if the buffer filled it writes `s[sz - 1] = 0` instead of preincrementing past the end. That prevents the staged 127-byte witness from reaching `line + 128`.

format.name: LibRaw Rollei header buffer
format.contract: A raw buffer that begins with `DSC-Image`, is exactly 127 bytes long, and contains no newline before EOF. On that path `identify()` dispatches to `parse_rollei()`, `parse_rollei()` calls `fgets(line, 128, ifp)` from offset 0, and the vulnerable `gets()` implementation exits with `pdest - str == 127` before writing the terminator with `*(++pdest) = 0`.
